newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX starts lower as Telekom slips.
newsitem.headline: German DAX starts lower as Telekom slips.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares, now including newly-floated Deutsche Telekom, started floor trade on Tuesday slightly lower as the new member lost some ground and weighed on the index.

Telekom shares, which traded for the first time on Monday in Europe's biggest initial public offering, lost over four percent, or 1.58 marks to trade down at 32.25, the lowest level since they started trading, but still well above the issue price of 28.50 marks.
Volumes in the market debutante were still strong, with over four million shares changing hands.
Dealers said players were taking profit in the stock and were divided over whether Telekom would stablise around current levels or try to climb higher.
Meanwhile, the DAX index, in which Telekom is now weighted at 4.5 percent, was down 2.24 points, or 0.08 percent at 2,761.60, fluctuating around its Monday closing level.

Dealers said most attention was still focused on Telekom, but figures out at German haircare and cosmetics group Wella AG and engineering group Mannesmann also attracted attention and weighed on both stocks.
Mannesmann was down 50 pfennigs at 622 marks in bourse trade with some analysts saying sales from its mobile telecommunications arm were seen as disappointing.

Preference shares in Wella tumbled nearly six percent, dropping 53 marks to 816 marks, after the group announced a drop in group pre-tax profit for the first nine months of the year to 84.4 million marks from 88.1 million.
Wella preference shares hit a day's low of 791 marks, but recovered some ground after the company said it expected profits to rise 25 percent next year.
